manifest.title: Docassemble
manifest.tagline: Guided interviews that assemble letters, forms and PDFs
manifest.description:
Docassemble runs guided interviews that ask people questions and assemble letters, forms and PDFs from
their answers. Interviews are written in YAML with optional Python, and authored in the built-in
Playground. It is widely used by legal aid organisations and courts.

This package runs docassemble on Cloudron's own PostgreSQL, Redis, mail and sign-in. Your
configuration, uploaded files and add-on packages live with the app's data and are included in
Cloudron backups.

**Who can run code.** Docassemble interviews can contain Python. Anyone with a developer or
administrator account can write and run that code in the Playground, and it runs with the same access
as the app itself, which includes every stored answer and account in this app's database. People who
only answer interviews cannot run code. Give developer and administrator roles only to people you
would trust with all of this app's data.
manifest.changelog:
* New package for docassemble 1.10.15, built from cloudron/base 6.0.1 with Python 3.15. It replaces the earlier v0.1 package and is a fresh install, not an update to it.
* Services come from Cloudron addons: PostgreSQL, Redis (also the background-task broker), LDAP sign-in, outgoing mail and scheduled jobs.
* config.yml is written once and kept; settings changed in docassemble's editor survive restarts.
* Live help: the websocket server now sends the Redis password.
* Sign-in with Cloudron accounts through LDAP (docassemble's WhoAmI check replaced; anonymous binds refused).
* PDFs use Tinos, metric-compatible with Times New Roman; STIX Two Text and Source Serif 4 included. Your own fonts go in /app/data/fonts.
* Background OCR returns text again (two upstream bugs fixed); background tasks no longer share database connections under load.
* Memory limit 4.5 GiB, measured.
* Thanks to timconsidine, whose community package first ran docassemble on Cloudron addons with Redis as the task broker.
manifest.postInstallMessage:
This app has its own administrator account, separate from your Cloudron account. Its email address
is `admin@` followed by this app's domain, and its password is generated for this install and kept in
`/app/data/.secrets/admin-password` (the checklist shows how to read it). Sign in with it first, then
change the password.

Cloudron users can sign in with their Cloudron email address and password. They start as ordinary users;
an administrator decides who becomes a developer.

### Developer accounts can see everything this app holds

Docassemble interviews are written in YAML and Python, and the Playground is where authors write and
test them. That Python runs inside this app with the same access as docassemble itself. In practice,
an interview author can read:

- every user's stored interview answers and account details, because the code can use the app's own
  database connection;
- uploaded files; and
- the app's mail settings.

It cannot reach other apps' databases, because Cloudron gives each app its own. Like any code on the
server, it can make network requests.

None of this applies to the people who answer your interviews: they only ever run what an author has
published. It applies to accounts with the **developer** or **administrator** role, and to any add-on
package an administrator installs.

So: give developer and administrator roles only to people you would trust with all of this app's
data, install add-on packages only from sources you trust, and use a separate docassemble app if you
need authors who should not see each other's users.

admin-password.message: Sign in as the docassemble administrator: the email is `admin@` followed by this app's domain, and the password is in `/app/data/.secrets/admin-password` (open a Terminal for this app with the `>_` button and run `cat /app/data/.secrets/admin-password`). Change the password after signing in.

roles.message: Cloudron users sign in with their Cloudron email address and start as ordinary users. Give the developer or administrator role only to people you would trust with all of this app's data (see the post-install notes).
